jp: 当店[とうてん]{は|wa-topic}現金[げんきん]{のみ/だけ|nomi-only}取[と]り扱[あつか]っております。
en: Our shop handles cash only.
why: のみ is the formal 'only'; しか needs a negative ending, and こそ or さえ would mean 'precisely' or 'even'.

jp: この部屋[へや]{は|wa-topic}会員[かいいん]{のみ/だけ|nomi-only}利用[りよう]できます。
en: Only members can use this room.
why: のみ limits the users to members alone; しか cannot end an affirmative verb, and も would add members to others.

jp: 立[た]ち入[い]り{は|wa-topic}関係者[かんけいしゃ]{のみ/だけ|nomi-only}{に|ni-recipient}許[ゆる]されています。
en: Entry is permitted to authorized personnel only.
why: のみ is the notice-style 'only' that restricts permission to one group; しか would need a negative verb.

jp: 応募[おうぼ]できる{の|no-nominalizer}{は/が|wa-topic}学生[がくせい]{のみ/だけ|nomi-only}です。
en: Only students can apply.
why: のみ before です marks students as the single eligible group; しか would need ありません.

jp: 今回[こんかい]{の|no-possessive}募集[ぼしゅう]{は|wa-topic}女性[じょせい]{のみ/だけ|nomi-only}対象[たいしょう]です。
en: This round of recruitment is for women only.
why: のみ restricts the target group to women alone; も would make women one target among others.

jp: 試験[しけん]{は|wa-topic}筆記[ひっき]{のみ/だけ|nomi-only}で、面接[めんせつ]{は/も|wa-negative}ありません。
en: The exam is written only; there is no interview.
why: のみ states that the written test is the whole exam, which is why no interview follows.

jp: 彼[かれ]{は|wa-topic}何[なに]{も|mo-total-negation}言[い]わず、ただうなずく{のみ/だけ|nomi-only}だった。
en: He said nothing and only nodded.
why: After a plain verb, のみ means that nodding was the only thing he did; しか does not fit before だった.

jp: 我々[われわれ]{は|wa-topic}結果[けっか]{を|o-object}待[ま]つ{のみ/だけ|nomi-only}です。
en: All we can do is wait for the result.
why: Verb plus のみです is the formal 'all there is left to do'; しか needs ありません instead of です.

jp: 本日[ほんじつ]{の|no-possessive}営業[えいぎょう]{は|wa-topic}午前[ごぜん]{のみ/だけ|nomi-only}です。
en: Today's business hours are the morning only.
why: のみ before です limits today's hours to the morning and excludes the afternoon.

jp: 社内[しゃない]{の|no-possessive}資料[しりょう]{は|wa-topic}、社員[しゃいん]{のみ/だけ|nomi-only}閲覧[えつらん]できます。
en: Internal documents can be viewed only by employees.
why: のみ makes employees the only people allowed to view; も would let employees and others view.

jp: 飲[の]み物[もの]{は|wa-topic}水[みず]{のみ/だけ|nomi-only}持[も]ち込[こ]めます。
en: Of drinks, only water may be brought in.
why: のみ allows water and nothing else; しか would need a negative verb such as 持ち込めません.

jp: 返品[へんぴん]{は|wa-topic}未開封[みかいふう]{の|no-possessive}商品[しょうひん]{のみ/だけ|nomi-only}承[うけたまわ]ります。
en: We accept returns of unopened items only.
why: のみ is the formal shop-notice 'only' for the one accepted category; しか would require a negative verb.

jp: この道[みち]{は|wa-topic}歩行者[ほこうしゃ]{のみ/だけ|nomi-only}通行[つうこう]できます。
en: Only pedestrians can pass along this road.
why: のみ restricts passage to pedestrians; も would let pedestrians through along with others.

jp: 本人[ほんにん]{のみ/だけ|nomi-only}{に|ni-recipient}書類[しょるい]{を|o-object}お渡[わた]しします。
en: We hand the documents only to the person themselves.
why: のみ singles out the person concerned as the only recipient; しか would need a negative verb.

jp: 私[わたし]{は|wa-topic}事実[じじつ]{のみ/だけ|nomi-only}{を|o-object}述[の]べます。
en: I will state only the facts.
why: のみ limits what I will say to facts; しか cannot go with an affirmative 述べます.

jp: 窓口[まどぐち]{は|wa-topic}平日[へいじつ]{のみ/だけ|nomi-only}開[あ]いています。
en: The counter is open on weekdays only.
why: のみ restricts the opening days to weekdays; しか would need 開いていません.

jp: 在庫[ざいこ]{は|wa-topic}店頭[てんとう]{のみ/だけ|nomi-only}{に|ni-location}ございます。
en: We have stock in the store only.
why: のみ limits the stock to the shop floor; しか would require the negative ございません.

jp: 薬[くすり]{は|wa-topic}痛[いた]い時[とき]{のみ/だけ|nomi-only}飲[の]んでください。
en: Please take the medicine only when it hurts.
why: のみ limits the permitted occasion to when you are in pain; しか cannot end a request with ください.

jp: その制度[せいど]{は|wa-topic}日本[にほん]{のみ/だけ|nomi-only}{に|ni-location}存在[そんざい]します。
en: That system exists only in Japan.
why: のみ says Japan is the only place the system exists; しか would need 存在しません.

jp: 先着[せんちゃく]十名[じゅうめい]様[さま]{のみ/だけ|nomi-only}{に|ni-recipient}記念品[きねんひん]{を|o-object}差[さ]し上[あ]げます。
en: We will give a souvenir only to the first ten customers.
why: のみ restricts the gift to the first ten customers; しか would need a negative verb.

jp: あと{は|wa-topic}署名[しょめい]{を|o-object}する{のみ/だけ|nomi-only}です。
en: All that remains is to sign.
why: Verb plus のみです means signing is the only step left; しか would need ありません.
